blocks.text: Dohra:

The royal consort who happened to be emperor's queen1 once, He happened to be the custodian at the same queen's court. Diley Ram2 was the name by which he was known, Lahore was the famous place which was his abode. (1)
lines: The royal consort who happened to be emperor's queen1 once,
He happened to be the custodian at the same queen's court.
Diley Ram2 was the name by which he was known,
Lahore was the famous place which was his abode.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As he had amassed a lot of wealth so skillfully, He had hidden a crore in cash out of that wealth. Countless other assets besides this amount did he possess, Jewellery worth several lakhs had he in his kitty. (2)
lines: As he had amassed a lot of wealth so skillfully,
He had hidden a crore in cash out of that wealth.
Countless other assets besides this amount did he possess,
Jewellery worth several lakhs had he in his kitty.

blocks.text: As his wealth could not be counted in thousands and hundreds, Listen to the manner fate dealt with this billionaire. Many a time Ahmed Shah Abdali invaded India from Kabul, Many a time did Delhi's emperor tried to repulse him. (3)
lines: As his wealth could not be counted in thousands and hundreds,
Listen to the manner fate dealt with this billionaire.
Many a time Ahmed Shah Abdali invaded India from Kabul,
Many a time did Delhi's emperor tried to repulse him.

blocks.text: Many a time had armed strife taken place there, Many a time had Lahore and Sirhind become theatres of war. Many an excess had the Muslims committed on the Singhs, So had a similar catastrophe befallen these two cities. (4)
lines: Many a time had armed strife taken place there,
Many a time had Lahore and Sirhind become theatres of war.
Many an excess had the Muslims committed on the Singhs,
So had a similar catastrophe befallen these two cities.

blocks.text: Dohra:

From the Deccan (South) descended the Marhattas, To fight the invader Abdali had the Marathas come. As both these aliens had mercenary intentions, The inhabitants of Lahore had to bear their brunt. (5)
lines: From the Deccan (South) descended the Marhattas,
To fight the invader Abdali had the Marathas come.
As both these aliens had mercenary intentions,
The inhabitants of Lahore had to bear their brunt.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As Marathas demanded wages from the Nawab (Adina Beg), He pressed the Lahore Nawab to meet the Maratha's demand. With this threat of being dispossessed of all his wealth, The Lahore Nawab invested his wealth with the Kasur financiers. (6)
lines: As Marathas demanded wages from the Nawab (Adina Beg),
He pressed the Lahore Nawab to meet the Maratha's demand.
With this threat of being dispossessed of all his wealth,
The Lahore Nawab invested his wealth with the Kasur financiers.

blocks.text: Sons of Dileram who happened to be in Lahore, They also transferred all their assets to Kasur. Out of the total one crore rupees that they had sent to Kasur, An amount worth five lacs was lost while in transit. (7)
lines: Sons of Dileram who happened to be in Lahore,
They also transferred all their assets to Kasur.
Out of the total one crore rupees that they had sent to Kasur,
An amount worth five lacs was lost while in transit.

blocks.text: Ornaments worth several lacs were dispatched to Kasur, As innumerable other assets too were transferred there. To Kasur, they sent their families as well for safety reasons, Considering Kasur to be safe and defiant to Abdali's invasions. (8)
lines: Ornaments worth several lacs were dispatched to Kasur,
As innumerable other assets too were transferred there.
To Kasur, they sent their families as well for safety reasons,
Considering Kasur to be safe and defiant to Abdali's invasions.

blocks.text: As this (ill-gotten) wealth was destined to destroy their lives. It became the immediate cause of their family's extinction. (9)
lines: As this (ill-gotten) wealth was destined to destroy their lives.
It became the immediate cause of their family's extinction.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The palatial mansion that belonged to Diley Ram, Was it ransacked by the Singhs in the first attempt. The moment the Singh chiefs heard about its immense treasures, Did they prohibit the public from entering this mansion. (10)
lines: The palatial mansion that belonged to Diley Ram,
Was it ransacked by the Singhs in the first attempt.
The moment the Singh chiefs heard about its immense treasures,
Did they prohibit the public from entering this mansion.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Earlier, the petty robbers had managed to enter this place, Thoroughly had they helped themselves with the valuables. As some carried bagfuls of valuables on their backs, Some others carried the robbed booty on their heads. (11)
lines: Earlier, the petty robbers had managed to enter this place,
Thoroughly had they helped themselves with the valuables.
As some carried bagfuls of valuables on their backs,
Some others carried the robbed booty on their heads.

blocks.text: Some found lots of silver others found plenty of gold, Whosoever entered this mansion felt fully rewarded. As these petty robbers carried valuables in bundles, Many a robber were dispossessed by the Khalsa chiefs. (12)
lines: Some found lots of silver others found plenty of gold,
Whosoever entered this mansion felt fully rewarded.
As these petty robbers carried valuables in bundles,
Many a robber were dispossessed by the Khalsa chiefs.

blocks.text: Then did the Singh chiefs realized the extent of hidden treasure, How much wealth had Diley Ram accumulated here. As the Singh chiefs seized and snatched these valuables, They came to possess a part of this hidden wealth. (13)
lines: Then did the Singh chiefs realized the extent of hidden treasure,
How much wealth had Diley Ram accumulated here.
As the Singh chiefs seized and snatched these valuables,
They came to possess a part of this hidden wealth.

blocks.text: Even the Singh chiefs could not keep hold on this wealth, As there were hardly any Singh soldiers to keep a guard. Wth all the Khalsa troops having gone on a looting spree, The Singh chiefs alone could not keep the robbers at bay. (14)
lines: Even the Singh chiefs could not keep hold on this wealth,
As there were hardly any Singh soldiers to keep a guard.
Wth all the Khalsa troops having gone on a looting spree,
The Singh chiefs alone could not keep the robbers at bay.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As the Singh troops returned having had their fill with plunder, They did assemble once again around their chiefs. Whatever hidden or buried treasure lay their inside, That also did the Singh chiefs keep under their siege. (15)
lines: As the Singh troops returned having had their fill with plunder,
They did assemble once again around their chiefs.
Whatever hidden or buried treasure lay their inside,
That also did the Singh chiefs keep under their siege.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The two Khalsa Misls belonging to Ramghrias and Ghanaiyas, Had had their camps at one and the same site. In two equal parts would they divide the plundered booty, Which served their interests well in equal measure. (16)
lines: The two Khalsa Misls belonging to Ramghrias and Ghanaiyas,
Had had their camps at one and the same site.
In two equal parts would they divide the plundered booty,
Which served their interests well in equal measure.

blocks.text: The way they kept on working in tandem with each other, So would I narrate their way of functioning together. As Ghanaiya chiefs3 came from a landlord's family of Kana village, Ramgharia's4 maternal parents belonged to that village. (17)
lines: The way they kept on working in tandem with each other,
So would I narrate their way of functioning together.
As Ghanaiya chiefs3 came from a landlord's family of Kana village,
Ramgharia's4 maternal parents belonged to that village.

blocks.text: This native link brought the two misl chiefs close to each other, The same filial affinity kept them united with each other. The son who was the oldest of Diley Ram's other sons, Was he put under house arrest by these Misl chiefs. The treasure that remained in possession of this eldest son Was the same confiscated by the two chiefs jointly. (18)
lines: This native link brought the two misl chiefs close to each other,
The same filial affinity kept them united with each other.
The son who was the oldest of Diley Ram's other sons,
Was he put under house arrest by these Misl chiefs.
The treasure that remained in possession of this eldest son Was the same confiscated by the two chiefs jointly.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Inflicting tortures and severe beatings on Diley Ram's eldest son, The two misl chiefs made him divulge the hidden treasures. Whosoever this captive son named as possessing wealth, Him did the chiefs order to be slaughtered instantly. (19)
lines: Inflicting tortures and severe beatings on Diley Ram's eldest son,
The two misl chiefs made him divulge the hidden treasures.
Whosoever this captive son named as possessing wealth,
Him did the chiefs order to be slaughtered instantly.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

All the hidden treasure did he bring out under duress, For this colossal wealth had he to stake his life. Being scared of losing his life in case he refused, He disclosed his entire wealth and its location. (20)
lines: All the hidden treasure did he bring out under duress,
For this colossal wealth had he to stake his life.
Being scared of losing his life in case he refused,
He disclosed his entire wealth and its location.

blocks.text: Being alive, he could survive even if he had to beg, Somehow or the other would he be able to earn. Being alive could one earn wealth once more, Thus did he save his life somehow or the other. (21)
lines: Being alive, he could survive even if he had to beg,
Somehow or the other would he be able to earn.
Being alive could one earn wealth once more,
Thus did he save his life somehow or the other.

blocks.text: Being alive, could he go on a pilgrimage to shrines, Being alive alone, could he meditate upon God's name. Propelled by such thoughts, did he manage to keep alive, Though the sinful (Ramgharias) killed this Dewan Diley Ram. (22)
lines: Being alive, could he go on a pilgrimage to shrines,
Being alive alone, could he meditate upon God's name.
Propelled by such thoughts, did he manage to keep alive,
Though the sinful (Ramgharias) killed this Dewan Diley Ram.

blocks.text: The way the Ramgharias' eliminated him, that would I narrate, The way they betrayed him, that would I state and record. The way the Ramgharias ruined themselves out of greed, The way the seized valuables remained unpossessed by them. (23)
lines: The way the Ramgharias' eliminated him, that would I narrate,
The way they betrayed him, that would I state and record.
The way the Ramgharias ruined themselves out of greed,
The way the seized valuables remained unpossessed by them.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Thus did Maali Singh5 again enquire from Diley Ram, Must he disclose the location of the hidden treaure.
The articles which were the most valuable among the whole treasure, Those alone would he (Maali Singh) pick up to place somewhere else. (24)
lines: The articles which were the most valuable among the whole treasure,
Those alone would he (Maali Singh) pick up to place somewhere else.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Enticing to reward him for his services of disclosure, Maali Singh promised to make Diley Ram his Misl's Dewan. Upon this, Diley Ram referred to a heavy box of steel, Which they had retrieved from beneath the stairs. (25)
lines: Enticing to reward him for his services of disclosure,
Maali Singh promised to make Diley Ram his Misl's Dewan.
Upon this,
Diley Ram referred to a heavy box of steel,
Which they had retrieved from beneath the stairs.

blocks.text: The most valuable jewellery did that steel box contain, Which the Ramgharias had locked in a small room. As this small room was well guarded from both the sides, How could Maali Singh lay his hands upon that box? (26)
lines: The most valuable jewellery did that steel box contain,
Which the Ramgharias had locked in a small room.
As this small room was well guarded from both the sides,
How could Maali Singh lay his hands upon that box?

blocks.text: Must he take hold of that box if he ever could take, Rest of the articles must he choose to ignore therein. All the jewels of Begum Noorjahan6 did that box contain, Must he take possession of that box if he wished to be rich. (27)
lines: Must he take hold of that box if he ever could take,
Rest of the articles must he choose to ignore therein.
All the jewels of Begum Noorjahan6 did that box contain,
Must he take possession of that box if he wished to be rich.

blocks.text: Such sparkling jewels did that box contain in it, That these shined as brilliantly as the moon at night. Such were crystalline diamonds studded with so many rubies, That these dazzled and attracted the onlooker at the first sight. (28)
lines: Such sparkling jewels did that box contain in it,
That these shined as brilliantly as the moon at night.
Such were crystalline diamonds studded with so many rubies,
That these dazzled and attracted the onlooker at the first sight.

blocks.text: White and pink rubies did twinkle as the twinkling stars, Some were as crimson red in hue as the pomegranate, Others were as deep blue as the feathers of a peacock, Still some others sparkled as green as the greenery around. (29)
lines: White and pink rubies did twinkle as the twinkling stars,
Some were as crimson red in hue as the pomegranate,
Others were as deep blue as the feathers of a peacock,
Still some others sparkled as green as the greenery around.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Thereupon, did Maali Singh ask Diley Ram to give details, Of the whole treasure that the steel box contained. Which specific articles of jewellery did it contain, Must Diley Ram provide specific details about those. (30)
lines: Thereupon, did Maali Singh ask Diley Ram to give details,
Of the whole treasure that the steel box contained.
Which specific articles of jewellery did it contain,
Must Diley Ram provide specific details about those.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereupon, whatever details he provided was impossible to narrate, Reams upon reams of paper would fail to contain their names. He could narrate their names had there been a few jewels, By the hundreds of names were those jewels known. (31)
lines: Thereupon, whatever details he provided was impossible to narrate,
Reams upon reams of paper would fail to contain their names.
He could narrate their names had there been a few jewels,
By the hundreds of names were those jewels known.

blocks.text: All these ornaments were cast in heavy gold, Many of these were carved and engraved in various designs. Many of these diamonds were meant to be necklaces, Several of these were in the form of nose pins and earnings. (32)
lines: All these ornaments were cast in heavy gold,
Many of these were carved and engraved in various designs.
Many of these diamonds were meant to be necklaces,
Several of these were in the form of nose pins and earnings.

blocks.text: Many of these were to be worn on hands and feet, Several of these were studded with diamonds and rubies. Many of these were rings studded with diamonds, Several of these were bracelets and crowns for the head. (33)
lines: Many of these were to be worn on hands and feet,
Several of these were studded with diamonds and rubies.
Many of these were rings studded with diamonds,
Several of these were bracelets and crowns for the head.

blocks.text: Decanters and goblets of gold were among these jewels, Pitchers made of gold studded with diamonds were there as well. How could he narrate the names of those innumerable jewels, Contented would he feel only if he could show these ornaments. (34)
lines: Decanters and goblets of gold were among these jewels,
Pitchers made of gold studded with diamonds were there as well.
How could he narrate the names of those innumerable jewels,
Contented would he feel only if he could show these ornaments.

blocks.text: Dohra:
The more Diley Ram talked about that hidden treasure, The more greedy did Maali Singh keep on becoming. The more avaricious a human being became, The less scared he felt of committing sins. (35)
lines: The more Diley Ram talked about that hidden treasure,
The more greedy did Maali Singh keep on becoming.
The more avaricious a human being became,
The less scared he felt of committing sins.

blocks.text: The moment Maali Singh Ramgharia heard about that box, And the contents that that box contained in it. Dazzled and out of his wits did he turn, And weakened in his moral scruples did he become. (36)
lines: The moment Maali Singh Ramgharia heard about that box,
And the contents that that box contained in it.
Dazzled and out of his wits did he turn,
And weakened in his moral scruples did he become.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The moment Malli Singh heard about that treasure, Inflamed with avarice he felt as if stung by a snake. As that poison (of avarice) poured into his system through his ears, How could it be cleansed without the services of a great psychoanalyst. (37)
lines: The moment Malli Singh heard about that treasure,
Inflamed with avarice he felt as if stung by a snake.
As that poison (of avarice) poured into his system through his ears,
How could it be cleansed without the services of a great psychoanalyst.

blocks.text: The more he thought about that valuable treasure, The more avaricious he became to acquire that wealth. All the moral scruples did he throw to the winds after hearing, All thoughts of morality and virtuous deeds did he abandon. (38)
lines: The more he thought about that valuable treasure,
The more avaricious he became to acquire that wealth.
All the moral scruples did he throw to the winds after hearing,
All thoughts of morality and virtuous deeds did he abandon.

blocks.text: Now sitting, now lying down under inflamed avarice, Moving to and fro then did he stand gripped with tension. Shaking and trembling with the unbearable tension, Finally did he proceed to S. Jassa Singh Ramgharia for a bargain. (39)
lines: Now sitting, now lying down under inflamed avarice,
Moving to and fro then did he stand gripped with tension.
Shaking and trembling with the unbearable tension,
Finally did he proceed to S.
Jassa Singh Ramgharia for a bargain.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Soon did Jassa Singh observe his younger brother Maali Singh, Rushing in great haste towards his own camp. Either was he coming with the foreboding of some mishap, Or had he found a bigger treasure in the old mansion. (40)
lines: Soon did Jassa Singh observe his younger brother Maali Singh,
Rushing in great haste towards his own camp.
Either was he coming with the foreboding of some mishap,
Or had he found a bigger treasure in the old mansion.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Maali Singh narrated the whole account he heard from (Diley Ram), About the huge treasure that he had found there. Never would he (Maali Singh) share that booty with the Ghnnaiyas, So must Jassa Singh suggest a strategy to conceal that treasure. (41)
lines: Maali Singh narrated the whole account he heard from (Diley Ram),
About the huge treasure that he had found there.
Never would he (Maali Singh) share that booty with the Ghnnaiyas,
So must Jassa Singh suggest a strategy to conceal that treasure.

blocks.text: Though Maali Singh dared not look at him in the eye, Jassa Singh forbade his brother from using such words. As Ramgharias and Ghannaiyas had taken vows to share things, How could the Ramgharias live after breaking those vows. (42)
lines: Though Maali Singh dared not look at him in the eye,
Jassa Singh forbade his brother from using such words.
As Ramgharias and Ghannaiyas had taken vows to share things,
How could the Ramgharias live after breaking those vows.

blocks.text: The wealth that one earns by backing out of one's vows, Ignominy does it bring besides the loss of such wealth. But never would Maali Singh budge from his new resolve, As his whole attention remained focused on that wealth. (43)
lines: The wealth that one earns by backing out of one's vows,
Ignominy does it bring besides the loss of such wealth.
But never would Maali Singh budge from his new resolve,
As his whole attention remained focused on that wealth.

blocks.text: Never could he live after sharing it with the Ghanaiyas, Surely would he stake his life for possessing that wealth. Ramgharias had occupied that ancient Mansion first, Though Jassa Singh had brought the Ghanaiyas there later on. (44)
lines: Never could he live after sharing it with the Ghanaiyas,
Surely would he stake his life for possessing that wealth.
Ramgharias had occupied that ancient Mansion first,
Though Jassa Singh had brought the Ghanaiyas there later on.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Then did Jassa Singh tell his younger brother, That he stood by his solemn pledge for the present. How did he know such a huge treasure lay hidden, In the old Mansion that belonged to Diley Ram. (45)
lines: Then did Jassa Singh tell his younger brother,
That he stood by his solemn pledge for the present.
How did he know such a huge treasure lay hidden,
In the old Mansion that belonged to Diley Ram.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Much did Jassa Singh try to persuade his brother, That transient and transitory was wealth indeed. A large fighting force did the ghanaiyas command, That united would all the Jat Sikhs stand against Ramgharias. (46)
lines: Much did Jassa Singh try to persuade his brother,
That transient and transitory was wealth indeed.
A large fighting force did the ghanaiyas command,
That united would all the Jat Sikhs stand against Ramgharias.

blocks.text: Hardly one percent troops did the Ramgharias command, Hundred times larger in strength were the Jat Sikh troops. Immensely would these Jat Sikhs harass the Ramgharias, As earlier had they killed a Ramgharia Khushal Singh7 . (47)
lines: Hardly one percent troops did the Ramgharias command,
Hundred times larger in strength were the Jat Sikh troops.
Immensely would these Jat Sikhs harass the Ramgharias,
As earlier had they killed a Ramgharia Khushal Singh7 .

blocks.text: That moment had passed with their brother's death : said Maali Sigh, Now nobody would sleep in peace after harming the Ramgharias. Begging his elder brother to let him keep that treasure, Maali Singh assured him of giving good fight to the whole Sikh Panth. (48)
lines: That moment had passed with their brother's death : said Maali Sigh,
Now nobody would sleep in peace after harming the Ramgharias.
Begging his elder brother to let him keep that treasure,
Maali Singh assured him of giving good fight to the whole Sikh Panth.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Then alone would Maali Singh keep his life, If Jassa Singh kept that wealth with themselves. Definitely would Maali Singh die fighting there, If his elder brother shared it with the Ghanaiyas. (49)
lines: Then alone would Maali Singh keep his life,
If Jassa Singh kept that wealth with themselves.
Definitely would Maali Singh die fighting there,
If his elder brother shared it with the Ghanaiyas.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

On the horns of dilemma was Jassa Singh indeed, He could either keep his faith or save his brother. Jassa Singh too got carried away by lust for wealth, As he saved his brother but breached his faith. (50)
lines: On the horns of dilemma was Jassa Singh indeed,
He could either keep his faith or save his brother.
Jassa Singh too got carried away by lust for wealth,
As he saved his brother but breached his faith.

blocks.text: Then did Jassa Singh chalk out a strategy, That Maali Singh must take over that wealth in secrecy. Diley Ram's son must be taken into confidence about it, That he must not disclose it to the Ghanaiyas. (51)
lines: Then did Jassa Singh chalk out a strategy,
That Maali Singh must take over that wealth in secrecy.
Diley Ram's son must be taken into confidence about it,
That he must not disclose it to the Ghanaiyas.

blocks.text: Both their faith and wealth would they lose, if disclosed, Surely would the Ghanaiyas snatch it after a fight. Thus did Maali Singh depart with this permission, Extremely delighted did he feel in his heart. (52)
lines: Both their faith and wealth would they lose, if disclosed,
Surely would the Ghanaiyas snatch it after a fight.
Thus did Maali Singh depart with this permission,
Extremely delighted did he feel in his heart.

blocks.text: Keeping awake through out the night (in excitement), Did he enter the old mansion with a force next morning. Distributing the other items after opening the dark cell, Maali Singh did take up the possession of the prized box. (53)
lines: Keeping awake through out the night (in excitement),
Did he enter the old mansion with a force next morning.
Distributing the other items after opening the dark cell,
Maali Singh did take up the possession of the prized box.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Declaring that the (prized) box had fallen into his share, Through deceit and force did he justify his claim. Lifting it amidst the noise of claims and counter claims, Despatched he the box of valuables to his own camp. (54)
lines: Declaring that the (prized) box had fallen into his share,
Through deceit and force did he justify his claim.
Lifting it amidst the noise of claims and counter claims,
Despatched he the box of valuables to his own camp.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
Thereupon arose a hue and cry from both the sides, As the Ghanaiyas arrived with a force to fight. Ramgharias being already prepared for a fight, Things reached a pitch for a violent encounter. (55)
lines: Thereupon arose a hue and cry from both the sides,
As the Ghanaiyas arrived with a force to fight.
Ramgharias being already prepared for a fight,
Things reached a pitch for a violent encounter.

blocks.text: Thereupon, some other Khalsa panth elders interceded, Focussing upon the real contentious issue above other issues. While the Ghanaiyas alleged the box contained a huge treasure, The Ramgharias declared nothing worthwhile had come out of it. (56)
lines: Thereupon, some other Khalsa panth elders interceded,
Focussing upon the real contentious issue above other issues.
While the Ghanaiyas alleged the box contained a huge treasure,
The Ramgharias declared nothing worthwhile had come out of it.

blocks.text: Thereafter, S. Charat Ssingh entering the fray to decide, He insisted on hearing Diley Ram's version about it. Thereupon, Maali Singh, entertaining a wicked thought, He thought of getting Diley Ram eliminated before hand. (57)
lines: Thereafter,
S.
Charat Ssingh entering the fray to decide,
He insisted on hearing Diley Ram's version about it.
Thereupon,
Maali Singh, entertaining a wicked thought,
He thought of getting Diley Ram eliminated before hand.

blocks.text: Thus did happen as the revered Guru had surmised, Sin, though evil, still endears one who is wicked. Cherishing this evil thought in his heart of hearts, The Ramgharias started thinking of committing this sin. (58)
lines: Thus did happen as the revered Guru had surmised,
Sin, though evil, still endears one who is wicked.
Cherishing this evil thought in his heart of hearts,
The Ramgharias started thinking of committing this sin.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Thereafter Maali Singh did think in his mind, Lest Diley Ram should disclose the box's contents. Both their honour and wealth being at stake of getting lost, They must take steps to preserve their honour and dignity. (59)
lines: Thereafter Maali Singh did think in his mind,
Lest Diley Ram should disclose the box's contents.
Both their honour and wealth being at stake of getting lost,
They must take steps to preserve their honour and dignity.

blocks.text: These sinful thoughts did not disturb their minds, That many a sinner had lost their honour through greed. One who keeps (someone's) wealth at home through sin, Rots he in hell forever never to get out of it. (60)
lines: These sinful thoughts did not disturb their minds,
That many a sinner had lost their honour through greed.
One who keeps (someone's) wealth at home through sin,
Rots he in hell forever never to get out of it.

blocks.text: This wicked (Ramgharia) thought of committing such a sin, That sends shivers down one's spine who hears of it. Calling a malcontent, Maali Singh gave him a brief, That he would get rewarded for killing Diley Ram. (61)
lines: This wicked (Ramgharia) thought of committing such a sin,
That sends shivers down one's spine who hears of it.
Calling a malcontent,
Maali Singh gave him a brief,
That he would get rewarded for killing Diley Ram.

blocks.text: Must he eliminate Diley Ram's (grandson) Hirday Ram8 , As his survival would upturn his whole game plan. Briefing how to make preparations for committing this murder, He asked him to behead him after smearing his head with curd. (62)
lines: Must he eliminate Diley Ram's (grandson) Hirday Ram8 ,
As his survival would upturn his whole game plan.
Briefing how to make preparations for committing this murder,
He asked him to behead him after smearing his head with curd.

blocks.text: Asking Diley Ram's grandson to pay him a visit, Maali Singh entreated him with a glib talk. Telling him about his having not washed himself for days, He made him wash his body in his own presence. (63)
lines: Asking Diley Ram's grandson to pay him a visit,
Maali Singh entreated him with a glib talk.
Telling him about his having not washed himself for days,
He made him wash his body in his own presence.

blocks.text: Making him bow down for cleaning his hair with curd, He got his head chopped of with a sword. Making the executioner run away from the scene, He declared the killer had escaped after that murder. (64)
lines: Making him bow down for cleaning his hair with curd,
He got his head chopped of with a sword.
Making the executioner run away from the scene,
He declared the killer had escaped after that murder.

blocks.text: Such a heinous crime did he commit indeed, That his stone -hearted heart did not feel scared. For this evil deed did the Ramgharia lose everything, Lose indeed they did their faith as well as wealth. (65)
lines: Such a heinous crime did he commit indeed,
That his stone -hearted heart did not feel scared.
For this evil deed did the Ramgharia lose everything,
Lose indeed they did their faith as well as wealth.

blocks.text: The same wealth did finally reach S. Charat Singh's Misl, For which the Ramgharias had betrayed the Ghanaiyas. Dear devout Sikh readers, listen to the whole account, As Rattan Singh had heard it and narrated it as such. (66)
lines: The same wealth did finally reach S.
Charat Singh's Misl,
For which the Ramgharias had betrayed the Ghanaiyas.
Dear devout Sikh readers, listen to the whole account,
As Rattan Singh had heard it and narrated it as such.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Plenty of wealth fell into Khalsa Panth's hands, Which wiped out all their want and indigence. The way Rattan Singh had heard of Kasur's ransacking, The same way had he recorded for his readers. (67)
lines: Plenty of wealth fell into Khalsa Panth's hands,
Which wiped out all their want and indigence.
The way Rattan Singh had heard of Kasur's ransacking,
The same way had he recorded for his readers.
